# 07 · Products: staff can rename a product

**Type:** Test coverage · **Area:** Catalogue / Products · **Priority:** Medium

## Context

Merchandisers rename products all the time (a season name, a spelling fix). The name is edited on
the product page and saved with the page's Save button; the page title follows the name. We have
no e2e coverage of the product page, and a rename that silently does not save is exactly the kind
of failure nobody notices until a customer does.

## What to cover

1. Open **E2E Hoodie** from the orders test data.
2. Change its name to "E2E Zip Hoodie" and save.
3. The product carries the new name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After saving, the page title shows "E2E Zip Hoodie".
- [ ] After a reload, the name field and the page title both show "E2E Zip Hoodie".

## Notes

- Use the existing orders test data; the product is already there.

import { e2eConfig } from "../../config.ts";
import { expect, test } from "../../fixtures/test.ts";
import { OrderPage } from "../../pages/orderPage.ts";
import { findOrderId, ORDERS_SCENARIO } from "../../scenarios/orders.ts";

/**
 * What happens to an order after it is placed. Replaces legacy SALEOR_77 and 80 (paid,
 * fulfilled, tracked - one lifecycle), SALEOR_78 (partial manual captures) and SALEOR_81
 * and 82 (address edits either side of fulfillment). SALEOR_79, the same lifecycle on the
 * deprecated payment (`Payment` object) flow, is deliberately not ported.
 */
test.use({ scenario: ORDERS_SCENARIO });

const config = e2eConfig();

test("Mark as paid, fulfill and add tracking #e2e", async ({ page }) => {
  // Arrange
  const orderPage = new OrderPage(page);

  await orderPage.goto(await findOrderId(config, "unpaid"));

  // Act & Assert
  await test.step("mark as paid", async () => {
    await orderPage.markAsPaid("e2e-reference");
    await expect(orderPage.paymentStatusBadges).toContainText("Fully charged");
    await expect(orderPage.transactions).toContainText("Mark-as-paid transaction");
  });

  await test.step("fulfill", async () => {
    await orderPage.fulfillAll();
    await expect(orderPage.statusInfo).toHaveText("Fulfilled");
  });

  await test.step("add tracking", async () => {
    await orderPage.addTracking("TRACK-123");
    await expect(orderPage.trackingNumber).toContainText("TRACK-123");
  });
});

test("Manual captures charge an order in parts #e2e", async ({ page }) => {
  // Arrange
  const orderPage = new OrderPage(page);

  await orderPage.goto(await findOrderId(config, "unpaid"));

  // Read rather than computed: the scenario's shipping method has a seeded, random price.
  const total = await orderPage.readTotal();
  const firstPart = 1;

  // Act & Assert
  await test.step("a capture below the total leaves the order partly charged", async () => {
    await orderPage.captureManually({ description: "first part", amount: firstPart });
    await expect(orderPage.paymentStatusBadges).toContainText("Not fully charged");
    await expect(orderPage.statusInfo).toHaveText("Unfulfilled");
  });

  await test.step("capturing the rest charges it fully", async () => {
    await orderPage.captureManually({ description: "second part", amount: total - firstPart });
    await expect(orderPage.paymentStatusBadges).toContainText("Fully charged");
    await expect(orderPage.transactions.getByText("Manual capture")).toHaveCount(2);
  });
});

test("Addresses stay editable before and after fulfillment #e2e", async ({ page }) => {
  // Arrange
  const orderPage = new OrderPage(page);
  const change = { firstName: "Grace", streetAddress1: "1 Main Street" };

  // Act & Assert
  await test.step("shipping address of an unfulfilled order", async () => {
    await orderPage.goto(await findOrderId(config, "unpaid"));
    await orderPage.editShippingAddressButton.click();
    await orderPage.addressDialog.changeAddress(change);
    await expect(orderPage.shippingAddressSection).toContainText(change.streetAddress1);
    await expect(orderPage.billingAddressSection).not.toContainText(change.streetAddress1);
  });

  await test.step("billing address of a fulfilled order", async () => {
    await orderPage.goto(await findOrderId(config, "fulfilled"));
    await expect(orderPage.statusInfo).toHaveText("Fulfilled");
    await orderPage.editBillingAddressButton.click();
    await orderPage.addressDialog.changeAddress(change);
    await expect(orderPage.billingAddressSection).toContainText(change.streetAddress1);
    await expect(orderPage.shippingAddressSection).not.toContainText(change.streetAddress1);
  });
});
# E2E conventions in the Saleor Dashboard suite

These are the rules a reviewer on the Saleor Dashboard team would hold a new `e2e/` spec to.
Every rule is taken from the suite as it stands (upstream commit `77dc49b`) and cites the file
that sets it. Nothing here is invented for this demo; where the suite only shows a habit rather
than stating a rule, that is said.

Paths are relative to the repository root.

## 1. Where tests live and how they start

**1.1 New specs go in `e2e/tests/`. `e2e-legacy/` is frozen.**
`docs/running-tests.md` ("New tests belong in `e2e/`"), `e2e/README.md` ("Porting from
`e2e-legacy/`": "It is frozen - do not edit it").

**1.2 Specs import `test` and `expect` from `e2e/fixtures/test.ts`, never from
`@playwright/test`.**
The suite's `test` is what restores the database and loads the actor's session
(`e2e/fixtures/test.ts:24-68`). A spec built on Playwright's own `test` gets neither: it runs on
whatever the previous test left behind, signed in as nobody. Every spec follows this
(`e2e/tests/orders/order-creation.spec.ts:1`, `e2e/tests/login.spec.ts:2`). `Page` and other
types may still be imported from `@playwright/test` (`e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:1`).

**1.3 Imports between suite files are relative and keep the `.ts` extension.**
`e2e/tsconfig.json:3-6` (type stripping under Node 24 needs it); every import in `e2e/`.

**1.4 Test titles describe the behaviour in a sentence and carry the `#e2e` tag.**
`e2e/tests/login.spec.ts:21`, `e2e/tests/orders/order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:16`. Area tags
may be added after it (`#translations` in `e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:88`).

**1.5 Each spec file opens with a comment saying what it covers and why.**
Every spec does this; the order specs also name the legacy cases they replace
(`e2e/tests/orders/draft-pricing.spec.ts:5-9`).

## 2. Test shape

**2.1 Arrange, Act, Assert are marked with comments.**
Repository rule in `CLAUDE.md` ("In tests, use `// Arrange`, `// Act`, and `// Assert`
comments"). Where acting and asserting interleave by stage, the suite writes
`// Act & Assert` (`e2e/tests/orders/order-creation.spec.ts:19`).

**2.2 One test is one user story, with a `test.step` per stage, so a failure names the stage.**
`e2e/tests/orders/order-creation.spec.ts:11` states it; `draft-pricing.spec.ts:30-47` and
`order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:23-37` follow it. Separate tests are for separate stories,
not for each assertion.

**2.3 Assertions are web-first: `await expect(locator).toHaveText(...)`, not
`expect(await locator.textContent())`.**
Every UI assertion in `e2e/tests/orders/`. Reading a value out of the page is reserved for when
the test needs the number for arithmetic, and is wrapped in a page-object method that says why
(`e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:95-98`, used at `order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:46-47`).

**2.4 Assert the outcome the story is about, not only that the UI responded.**
The order specs check the resulting status, totals and sections after each action
(`order-creation.spec.ts:38-41`, `order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:29-32`). Where persistence
is the point, the suite proves it: a reload (`productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:117-120`) or a read
through the API (`productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:148-164`). A test whose assertions would
still pass with the feature broken is not doing its job.

**2.5 Expected values come from the scenario's exported constants, and arithmetic is guarded.**
`draft-pricing.spec.ts:16-25` derives every expected amount from `PRODUCTS` and `PROMOTIONS`
(`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:41-50`) and asserts the preconditions its maths relies on. Values that
the seed randomises are read from the page instead, with a comment saying so
(`order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:46`).

**2.6 Money is compared as `amount.toFixed(2)`.**
`draft-pricing.spec.ts:12`, `e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:74`. The dashboard renders totals without a
currency symbol (`e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:95`).

## 3. Data: scenarios, not set-up code

**3.1 A test starts from a named scenario: `test.use({ scenario: ... })`.**
`e2e/fixtures/test.ts:26` (default `"default"`, Saleor's `populatedb`);
`e2e/tests/orders/order-creation.spec.ts:13`. The scenario name is imported from the scenario
file, not typed as a string (`ORDERS_SCENARIO`, `e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:18`).

**3.2 State a spec needs is a scenario, built once and restored, not something the spec creates
on the way past.**
`e2e/README.md` ("Isolation, and opting into parallel": "a state a spec needs is a scenario,
named and built, not something the spec creates on the way past"). The one exception the suite
makes is a draft order: drafts are cheap to start through the UI, and the draft specs do that in
their Arrange step with the existing page-object flow (`DraftOrderPage.create`,
`e2e/tests/orders/draft-pricing.spec.ts:27`). Arranging through direct API mutations inside a
spec, in a `beforeEach`, or re-creating something a scenario already holds (a new order when the
scenario has the unpaid one) is not the pattern.

**3.3 Use what the existing scenarios already provide before adding one.**
`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts` provides known products and prices, one customer, both promotion types
and an unpaid and a fulfilled order (`orders.ts:6-61`). A spec that needs one of these uses it.

**3.4 A new scenario builds on `default` with `parent: "default"`, goes through the GraphQL API,
fails loudly on mutation errors, and is registered.**
`e2e/README.md` ("Seeds are built, not written"), `e2e/scenarios/scenario.ts:10-23`,
`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:342-345` (`parent`), `orders.ts:71-80` and
`e2e/lib/graphql.ts:55-63` (`assertNoMutationErrors`), `e2e/scenarios/registry.ts`. Raw SQL is
only for states the API cannot express (`e2e/scenarios/scenario.ts:10-13`).

**3.5 No hard-coded ids. Look rows up at test time by a stable key.**
Ids change with every build of the dump. `findOrderId` finds orders by `e2e` metadata
(`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:52-55`, `391-411`). Reads like this are safe at test time; writes are
not (3.2).

**3.6 Do not depend on what `populatedb` happens to generate.**
Its orders, customers and promotions are random (`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:9-16`). A spec that
asserts on a populatedb product name, price or order number will break on the next seed build.

**3.7 GraphQL from test code goes through `e2e/lib/graphql.ts`.**
`gql`, `signIn`, `adminToken` and `assertNoMutationErrors` (`e2e/lib/graphql.ts`). No hand-rolled
`fetch` against the API, no second copy of these helpers.

## 4. Isolation and cleanup

**4.1 The database is restored before every test, so specs carry no cleanup code and no
unique-name tricks.**
`e2e/README.md` ("Specs need no cleanup discipline and no unique names, and nothing in the seed
is ever consumed"), `e2e/fixtures/test.ts:28-55`. `afterEach` deletes, timestamped names and
"delete if exists" steps are noise here, and a sign the author did not know how the suite works.

**4.2 Nothing may outlive the test's own reset.**
What _can_ leave data behind in this suite: tagging a test that writes as `parallel()` (its group
shares one database, `e2e/config.ts:48-74`), writing to the scenario dumps or the cached sessions
under `e2e/.cache/` at test time (`e2e/lib/seed.ts:17`), or changing seed state from global setup. Each of these
leaks into later tests.

**4.3 `parallel()` is only for blocks that read without writing, and never for tests that sign in
through the UI.**
`e2e/config.ts:48-74`, `e2e/README.md` ("What cannot be tagged: signing in").

**4.4 No retries, and no per-test changes to timeouts without a stated reason.**
`e2e/playwright.config.ts:84-90` (`retries: 0`: "a retry mostly hides a real defect"),
`playwright.config.ts:103-110` (`actionTimeout`, `expect` timeout).

## 5. Actors

**5.1 Pick who is signed in with `test.use({ actor: ... })`. The default is `admin`.**
`e2e/fixtures/test.ts:25`, `e2e/README.md` ("Actors"), `e2e/lib/actors.ts:13-28`.

**5.2 Do not sign in through the UI except in the login spec. `anonymous` is for that.**
Stored sessions are loaded by the fixture (`e2e/fixtures/test.ts:57-67`); UI sign-in is
throttled per IP (`e2e/README.md`, "What cannot be tagged: signing in"). `e2e/tests/login.spec.ts`
is the one spec that signs in itself.

**5.3 Permission stories use the single-permission actor for that permission.**
`e2e/lib/actors.ts:3-28`; `e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:261-275` uses
`translations` and checks its permissions.

**5.4 Credentials come from `e2e/config.ts` and `e2e/lib/actors.ts`, never literals in a spec.**
`ADMIN`, `STAFF_PASSWORD`, `credentialsFor` (`e2e/config.ts:43-46`, `e2e/lib/actors.ts:38-50`).

## 6. Locators and page objects

**6.1 Locate by `data-test-id` with `getByTestId`; otherwise by role and accessible name.**
`e2e/playwright.config.ts:105` (`testIdAttribute: "data-test-id"`); `e2e/README.md` ("The
locators are `data-test-id`s"). Role locators where no test id exists
(`e2e/pages/addressDialog.ts:23-27`). No CSS class selectors, no XPath, no `nth-child`, no text of
generated ids. `.filter({ hasText })` narrows a test-id list to the row wanted
(`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts:85-88`).

**6.2 Scope locators to the container they belong to.**
Dialog buttons are found inside the dialog (`this.dialog.getByTestId("submit")`,
`e2e/pages/addressDialog.ts:49`, `e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:67`), because `submit` exists on many
screens.

**6.3 Locators live in page objects in `e2e/pages/`, as `readonly` fields initialised from
`this.page`, with `constructor(readonly page: Page) {}`.**
`e2e/README.md` ("Porting": "Locators become `readonly` class fields initialized from
`this.page`, with an empty `constructor(readonly page: Page) {}`"); `e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:10-57`.
Specs call page-object methods and assert on page-object locators. The suite's one inline helper
(`saveAlt` in `e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:81-86`) predates this and is not the
pattern to copy.

**6.4 Reuse the page object that already covers the screen, and extend it there.**
`DraftOrderPage` covers drafts (`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts`), `OrderPage` placed orders
(`e2e/pages/orderPage.ts`), `AddressDialog` the address dialog both open
(`e2e/pages/addressDialog.ts`, composed at `draftOrderPage.ts:12` and `orderPage.ts:11`). A new
action on an order belongs on `OrderPage`, not in a second class or a spec-local helper. A new
page object is for a screen no existing one covers.

**6.5 Page-object methods are named for the user's action and carry a comment when they handle
something non-obvious.**
`addProduct`, `assignCustomer`, `fulfillAll`, `markAsPaid`; the comments at
`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts:76-80` and `e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:79` explain why the method waits
the way it does.

## 7. Waiting

**7.1 No fixed waits. No `waitForTimeout`, no `setTimeout` sleeps.**
Nowhere in `e2e/tests/` or `e2e/pages/`. The suite waits on something it can name.

**7.2 Wait on the UI state that proves the step finished.**
A web-first assertion (`await expect(this.statusInfo).toHaveText("Draft")`,
`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts:73`), a dialog closing (`this.dialog.waitFor({ state: "hidden" })`,
`e2e/pages/addressDialog.ts:84`), a URL change (`page.waitForURL(...)`,
`e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:82-84`), or a list settling before acting in it
(`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts:84`).

**7.3 Waiting on network responses is for asserting on the response itself.**
`e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:231-246` waits for one named GraphQL operation because
the test asserts on its error payload. The suite never uses `networkidle`.

## 8. Code quality

**8.1 Strict TypeScript; no `any`; typed GraphQL responses.**
`e2e/tsconfig.json:18` (`strict`), repository `CLAUDE.md` ("strict TypeScript"), `gql<T>`
(`e2e/lib/graphql.ts:23`). The repository's Claude hooks also block `as any`
(`.claude/hooks/check-as-any-pre.py`).

**8.2 It type-checks and lints.**
`pnpm run check-types:e2e` (`package.json`), and the repository lint (`CLAUDE.md`,
"Verification").

**8.3 Comments explain why, not what.**
Every comment in `e2e/pages/` and `e2e/tests/orders/` explains a reason (a wait, a dropped
assertion, a value read rather than computed). Comments narrating the next line are not the
house style.
# Review checklist for an AI-written e2e test

Used to review every test in this demo, from both branches, the same way. Each item comes from
[CONVENTIONS.md](CONVENTIONS.md); the number in brackets is the convention it enforces.

- **Blocker**: the test should not merge until this is fixed. It is wrong, misleading, flaky by
  construction, or makes the suite worse.
- **Minor**: the test works but does not read like the rest of the suite. A reviewer would ask
  for it to be changed, but would not refuse the merge over it alone.

How findings are counted is in [SCORING.md](SCORING.md): each item is judged once per ticket,
across everything that ticket's change adds or edits (spec, page objects, scenarios).

## Blockers

| ID  | Check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Conventions        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| B1  | **Would pass with the feature broken.** If the behaviour in the ticket stopped working, at least one assertion would fail. Fails if the assertions only prove the UI responded (a dialog closed, a toast appeared, a button was clicked) and not the outcome, or if they are made on values the action never changes.                                                                             | 2.4                |
| B2  | **Misses an acceptance criterion.** Every acceptance criterion in the ticket is asserted somewhere.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 2.4                |
| B3  | **Duplicates a helper that exists.** No second copy of something the suite already has: a locator or action already on `DraftOrderPage`, `OrderPage`, `AddressDialog`, `HomePage` or `LoginPage`; a GraphQL helper in `e2e/lib/graphql.ts`; a lookup like `findOrderId`; a scenario constant like `PRODUCTS` or `CUSTOMER`. Includes a new page-object class for a screen an existing one covers. | 3.3, 3.7, 6.4      |
| B4  | **Hard wait.** No `waitForTimeout`, `setTimeout`-based sleep, or polling loop with a fixed delay.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | 7.1                |
| B5  | **Leaves data behind or bypasses the reset.** Uses Playwright's own `test` instead of `e2e/fixtures/test.ts` (no reset, no actor); tags a writing test `parallel()`; writes to `e2e/.cache/`, the dumps or the stored sessions; changes seed state outside a registered scenario.                                                                                                                 | 1.2, 4.2, 4.3      |
| B6  | **Selectors ignore the suite's locator rules.** Uses CSS class selectors, XPath, `nth-child`/positional indexes as the way to find an element, or generated ids, where a `data-test-id` or role-and-name locator exists or could be used. Includes unscoped `getByTestId("submit")`-style locators that match on more than one part of the screen.                                                | 6.1, 6.2           |
| B7  | **Arranges state inside the spec.** Creates or changes the data it needs through API calls in the spec, in `beforeEach`, or through the UI, when an existing scenario provides it or a scenario should. Starting a draft with the existing `DraftOrderPage.create` flow is the suite's own pattern and is fine.                                                                                   | 3.1, 3.2, 3.3      |
| B8  | **Depends on unstable data.** Hard-codes database ids, or asserts on values `populatedb` randomises (its product names, prices, order numbers, customers) instead of the scenario's known values.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | 2.5, 3.5, 3.6      |
| B9  | **Signs in through the UI, or with the wrong actor.** Logs in via the login form outside `login.spec.ts`; uses `admin` for a story the ticket gives to a specific permission; types credentials into a spec.                                                                                                                                                                                      | 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4 |
| B10 | **Does not compile, or lives in the wrong place.** Fails `pnpm run check-types:e2e`; is written under `e2e-legacy/` or outside `e2e/tests/`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 1.1, 8.2           |

## Minors

# E2E conventions in the Saleor Dashboard suite

These are the rules a reviewer on the Saleor Dashboard team would hold a new `e2e/` spec to.
Every rule is taken from the suite as it stands (upstream commit `77dc49b`) and cites the file
that sets it. Nothing here is invented for this demo; where the suite only shows a habit rather
than stating a rule, that is said.

Paths are relative to the repository root.

## 1. Where tests live and how they start

**1.1 New specs go in `e2e/tests/`. `e2e-legacy/` is frozen.**
`docs/running-tests.md` ("New tests belong in `e2e/`"), `e2e/README.md` ("Porting from
`e2e-legacy/`": "It is frozen - do not edit it").

**1.2 Specs import `test` and `expect` from `e2e/fixtures/test.ts`, never from
`@playwright/test`.**
The suite's `test` is what restores the database and loads the actor's session
(`e2e/fixtures/test.ts:24-68`). A spec built on Playwright's own `test` gets neither: it runs on
whatever the previous test left behind, signed in as nobody. Every spec follows this
(`e2e/tests/orders/order-creation.spec.ts:1`, `e2e/tests/login.spec.ts:2`). `Page` and other
types may still be imported from `@playwright/test` (`e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:1`).

**1.3 Imports between suite files are relative and keep the `.ts` extension.**
`e2e/tsconfig.json:3-6` (type stripping under Node 24 needs it); every import in `e2e/`.

**1.4 Test titles describe the behaviour in a sentence and carry the `#e2e` tag.**
`e2e/tests/login.spec.ts:21`, `e2e/tests/orders/order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:16`. Area tags
may be added after it (`#translations` in `e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:88`).

**1.5 Each spec file opens with a comment saying what it covers and why.**
Every spec does this; the order specs also name the legacy cases they replace
(`e2e/tests/orders/draft-pricing.spec.ts:5-9`).

## 2. Test shape

**2.1 Arrange, Act, Assert are marked with comments.**
Repository rule in `CLAUDE.md` ("In tests, use `// Arrange`, `// Act`, and `// Assert`
comments"). Where acting and asserting interleave by stage, the suite writes
`// Act & Assert` (`e2e/tests/orders/order-creation.spec.ts:19`).

**2.2 One test is one user story, with a `test.step` per stage, so a failure names the stage.**
`e2e/tests/orders/order-creation.spec.ts:11` states it; `draft-pricing.spec.ts:30-47` and
`order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:23-37` follow it. Separate tests are for separate stories,
not for each assertion.

**2.3 Assertions are web-first: `await expect(locator).toHaveText(...)`, not
`expect(await locator.textContent())`.**
Every UI assertion in `e2e/tests/orders/`. Reading a value out of the page is reserved for when
the test needs the number for arithmetic, and is wrapped in a page-object method that says why
(`e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:95-98`, used at `order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:46-47`).

**2.4 Assert the outcome the story is about, not only that the UI responded.**
The order specs check the resulting status, totals and sections after each action
(`order-creation.spec.ts:38-41`, `order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:29-32`). Where persistence
is the point, the suite proves it: a reload (`productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:117-120`) or a read
through the API (`productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:148-164`). A test whose assertions would
still pass with the feature broken is not doing its job.

**2.5 Expected values come from the scenario's exported constants, and arithmetic is guarded.**
`draft-pricing.spec.ts:16-25` derives every expected amount from `PRODUCTS` and `PROMOTIONS`
(`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:41-50`) and asserts the preconditions its maths relies on. Values that
the seed randomises are read from the page instead, with a comment saying so
(`order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts:46`).

**2.6 Money is compared as `amount.toFixed(2)`.**
`draft-pricing.spec.ts:12`, `e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:74`. The dashboard renders totals without a
currency symbol (`e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:95`).

## 3. Data: scenarios, not set-up code

**3.1 A test starts from a named scenario: `test.use({ scenario: ... })`.**
`e2e/fixtures/test.ts:26` (default `"default"`, Saleor's `populatedb`);
`e2e/tests/orders/order-creation.spec.ts:13`. The scenario name is imported from the scenario
file, not typed as a string (`ORDERS_SCENARIO`, `e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:18`).

**3.2 State a spec needs is a scenario, built once and restored, not something the spec creates
on the way past.**
`e2e/README.md` ("Isolation, and opting into parallel": "a state a spec needs is a scenario,
named and built, not something the spec creates on the way past"). The one exception the suite
makes is a draft order: drafts are cheap to start through the UI, and the draft specs do that in
their Arrange step with the existing page-object flow (`DraftOrderPage.create`,
`e2e/tests/orders/draft-pricing.spec.ts:27`). Arranging through direct API mutations inside a
spec, in a `beforeEach`, or re-creating something a scenario already holds (a new order when the
scenario has the unpaid one) is not the pattern.

**3.3 Use what the existing scenarios already provide before adding one.**
`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts` provides known products and prices, one customer, both promotion types
and an unpaid and a fulfilled order (`orders.ts:6-61`). A spec that needs one of these uses it.

**3.4 A new scenario builds on `default` with `parent: "default"`, goes through the GraphQL API,
fails loudly on mutation errors, and is registered.**
`e2e/README.md` ("Seeds are built, not written"), `e2e/scenarios/scenario.ts:10-23`,
`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:342-345` (`parent`), `orders.ts:71-80` and
`e2e/lib/graphql.ts:55-63` (`assertNoMutationErrors`), `e2e/scenarios/registry.ts`. Raw SQL is
only for states the API cannot express (`e2e/scenarios/scenario.ts:10-13`).

**3.5 No hard-coded ids. Look rows up at test time by a stable key.**
Ids change with every build of the dump. `findOrderId` finds orders by `e2e` metadata
(`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:52-55`, `391-411`). Reads like this are safe at test time; writes are
not (3.2).

**3.6 Do not depend on what `populatedb` happens to generate.**
Its orders, customers and promotions are random (`e2e/scenarios/orders.ts:9-16`). A spec that
asserts on a populatedb product name, price or order number will break on the next seed build.

**3.7 GraphQL from test code goes through `e2e/lib/graphql.ts`.**
`gql`, `signIn`, `adminToken` and `assertNoMutationErrors` (`e2e/lib/graphql.ts`). No hand-rolled
`fetch` against the API, no second copy of these helpers.

## 4. Isolation and cleanup

**4.1 The database is restored before every test, so specs carry no cleanup code and no
unique-name tricks.**
`e2e/README.md` ("Specs need no cleanup discipline and no unique names, and nothing in the seed
is ever consumed"), `e2e/fixtures/test.ts:28-55`. `afterEach` deletes, timestamped names and
"delete if exists" steps are noise here, and a sign the author did not know how the suite works.

**4.2 Nothing may outlive the test's own reset.**
What _can_ leave data behind in this suite: tagging a test that writes as `parallel()` (its group
shares one database, `e2e/config.ts:48-74`), writing to the scenario dumps or the cached sessions
under `e2e/.cache/` at test time (`e2e/lib/seed.ts:17`), or changing seed state from global setup. Each of these
leaks into later tests.

**4.3 `parallel()` is only for blocks that read without writing, and never for tests that sign in
through the UI.**
`e2e/config.ts:48-74`, `e2e/README.md` ("What cannot be tagged: signing in").

**4.4 No retries, and no per-test changes to timeouts without a stated reason.**
`e2e/playwright.config.ts:84-90` (`retries: 0`: "a retry mostly hides a real defect"),
`playwright.config.ts:103-110` (`actionTimeout`, `expect` timeout).

## 5. Actors

**5.1 Pick who is signed in with `test.use({ actor: ... })`. The default is `admin`.**
`e2e/fixtures/test.ts:25`, `e2e/README.md` ("Actors"), `e2e/lib/actors.ts:13-28`.

**5.2 Do not sign in through the UI except in the login spec. `anonymous` is for that.**
Stored sessions are loaded by the fixture (`e2e/fixtures/test.ts:57-67`); UI sign-in is
throttled per IP (`e2e/README.md`, "What cannot be tagged: signing in"). `e2e/tests/login.spec.ts`
is the one spec that signs in itself.

**5.3 Permission stories use the single-permission actor for that permission.**
`e2e/lib/actors.ts:3-28`; `e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:261-275` uses
`translations` and checks its permissions.

**5.4 Credentials come from `e2e/config.ts` and `e2e/lib/actors.ts`, never literals in a spec.**
`ADMIN`, `STAFF_PASSWORD`, `credentialsFor` (`e2e/config.ts:43-46`, `e2e/lib/actors.ts:38-50`).

## 6. Locators and page objects

**6.1 Locate by `data-test-id` with `getByTestId`; otherwise by role and accessible name.**
`e2e/playwright.config.ts:105` (`testIdAttribute: "data-test-id"`); `e2e/README.md` ("The
locators are `data-test-id`s"). Role locators where no test id exists
(`e2e/pages/addressDialog.ts:23-27`). No CSS class selectors, no XPath, no `nth-child`, no text of
generated ids. `.filter({ hasText })` narrows a test-id list to the row wanted
(`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts:85-88`).

**6.2 Scope locators to the container they belong to.**
Dialog buttons are found inside the dialog (`this.dialog.getByTestId("submit")`,
`e2e/pages/addressDialog.ts:49`, `e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:67`), because `submit` exists on many
screens.

**6.3 Locators live in page objects in `e2e/pages/`, as `readonly` fields initialised from
`this.page`, with `constructor(readonly page: Page) {}`.**
`e2e/README.md` ("Porting": "Locators become `readonly` class fields initialized from
`this.page`, with an empty `constructor(readonly page: Page) {}`"); `e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:10-57`.
Specs call page-object methods and assert on page-object locators. The suite's one inline helper
(`saveAlt` in `e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:81-86`) predates this and is not the
pattern to copy.

**6.4 Reuse the page object that already covers the screen, and extend it there.**
`DraftOrderPage` covers drafts (`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts`), `OrderPage` placed orders
(`e2e/pages/orderPage.ts`), `AddressDialog` the address dialog both open
(`e2e/pages/addressDialog.ts`, composed at `draftOrderPage.ts:12` and `orderPage.ts:11`). A new
action on an order belongs on `OrderPage`, not in a second class or a spec-local helper. A new
page object is for a screen no existing one covers.

**6.5 Page-object methods are named for the user's action and carry a comment when they handle
something non-obvious.**
`addProduct`, `assignCustomer`, `fulfillAll`, `markAsPaid`; the comments at
`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts:76-80` and `e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:79` explain why the method waits
the way it does.

## 7. Waiting

**7.1 No fixed waits. No `waitForTimeout`, no `setTimeout` sleeps.**
Nowhere in `e2e/tests/` or `e2e/pages/`. The suite waits on something it can name.

**7.2 Wait on the UI state that proves the step finished.**
A web-first assertion (`await expect(this.statusInfo).toHaveText("Draft")`,
`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts:73`), a dialog closing (`this.dialog.waitFor({ state: "hidden" })`,
`e2e/pages/addressDialog.ts:84`), a URL change (`page.waitForURL(...)`,
`e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:82-84`), or a list settling before acting in it
(`e2e/pages/draftOrderPage.ts:84`).

**7.3 Waiting on network responses is for asserting on the response itself.**
`e2e/tests/productMediaTranslations.spec.ts:231-246` waits for one named GraphQL operation because
the test asserts on its error payload. The suite never uses `networkidle`.

## 8. Code quality

**8.1 Strict TypeScript; no `any`; typed GraphQL responses.**
`e2e/tsconfig.json:18` (`strict`), repository `CLAUDE.md` ("strict TypeScript"), `gql<T>`
(`e2e/lib/graphql.ts:23`). The repository's Claude hooks also block `as any`
(`.claude/hooks/check-as-any-pre.py`).

**8.2 It type-checks and lints.**
`pnpm run check-types:e2e` (`package.json`), and the repository lint (`CLAUDE.md`,
"Verification").

**8.3 Comments explain why, not what.**
Every comment in `e2e/pages/` and `e2e/tests/orders/` explains a reason (a wait, a dropped
assertion, a value read rather than computed). Comments narrating the next line are not the
house style.
# Review checklist for an AI-written e2e test

Used to review every test in this demo, from both branches, the same way. Each item comes from
[CONVENTIONS.md](CONVENTIONS.md); the number in brackets is the convention it enforces.

- **Blocker**: the test should not merge until this is fixed. It is wrong, misleading, flaky by
  construction, or makes the suite worse.
- **Minor**: the test works but does not read like the rest of the suite. A reviewer would ask
  for it to be changed, but would not refuse the merge over it alone.

How findings are counted is in [SCORING.md](SCORING.md): each item is judged once per ticket,
across everything that ticket's change adds or edits (spec, page objects, scenarios).

## Blockers

| ID  | Check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Conventions        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| B1  | **Would pass with the feature broken.** If the behaviour in the ticket stopped working, at least one assertion would fail. Fails if the assertions only prove the UI responded (a dialog closed, a toast appeared, a button was clicked) and not the outcome, or if they are made on values the action never changes.                                                                             | 2.4                |
| B2  | **Misses an acceptance criterion.** Every acceptance criterion in the ticket is asserted somewhere.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 2.4                |
| B3  | **Duplicates a helper that exists.** No second copy of something the suite already has: a locator or action already on `DraftOrderPage`, `OrderPage`, `AddressDialog`, `HomePage` or `LoginPage`; a GraphQL helper in `e2e/lib/graphql.ts`; a lookup like `findOrderId`; a scenario constant like `PRODUCTS` or `CUSTOMER`. Includes a new page-object class for a screen an existing one covers. | 3.3, 3.7, 6.4      |
| B4  | **Hard wait.** No `waitForTimeout`, `setTimeout`-based sleep, or polling loop with a fixed delay.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | 7.1                |
| B5  | **Leaves data behind or bypasses the reset.** Uses Playwright's own `test` instead of `e2e/fixtures/test.ts` (no reset, no actor); tags a writing test `parallel()`; writes to `e2e/.cache/`, the dumps or the stored sessions; changes seed state outside a registered scenario.                                                                                                                 | 1.2, 4.2, 4.3      |
| B6  | **Selectors ignore the suite's locator rules.** Uses CSS class selectors, XPath, `nth-child`/positional indexes as the way to find an element, or generated ids, where a `data-test-id` or role-and-name locator exists or could be used. Includes unscoped `getByTestId("submit")`-style locators that match on more than one part of the screen.                                                | 6.1, 6.2           |
| B7  | **Arranges state inside the spec.** Creates or changes the data it needs through API calls in the spec, in `beforeEach`, or through the UI, when an existing scenario provides it or a scenario should. Starting a draft with the existing `DraftOrderPage.create` flow is the suite's own pattern and is fine.                                                                                   | 3.1, 3.2, 3.3      |
| B8  | **Depends on unstable data.** Hard-codes database ids, or asserts on values `populatedb` randomises (its product names, prices, order numbers, customers) instead of the scenario's known values.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | 2.5, 3.5, 3.6      |
| B9  | **Signs in through the UI, or with the wrong actor.** Logs in via the login form outside `login.spec.ts`; uses `admin` for a story the ticket gives to a specific permission; types credentials into a spec.                                                                                                                                                                                      | 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4 |
| B10 | **Does not compile, or lives in the wrong place.** Fails `pnpm run check-types:e2e`; is written under `e2e-legacy/` or outside `e2e/tests/`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 1.1, 8.2           |

## Minors

| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| M1  | **Locators defined in the spec.** Locators or multi-step UI actions written inline in the spec rather than on the page object that covers the screen (when it is not already a B3 duplicate).                   | 6.3, 6.4      |
| M2  | **Page-object style.** New page-object members are not `readonly` fields initialised from `this.page`, or the class does not use `constructor(readonly page: Page) {}`.                                         | 6.3           |
| M3  | **No Arrange / Act / Assert comments.**                                                                                                                                                                         | 2.1           |
| M4  | **Not one story with steps.** Several stages in one test without `test.step`, or one story split across tests that each repeat the set-up.                                                                      | 2.2           |
| M5  | **Title or tag.** Title does not say what behaviour is checked, or the `#e2e` tag is missing.                                                                                                                   | 1.4           |
| M6  | **No header comment** saying what the spec covers and why.                                                                                                                                                      | 1.5           |
| M7  | **Not web-first.** Reads text or state out of the page and asserts on the copy (`expect(await x.textContent())`, `isVisible()` in an `if`/`expect`) where a web-first assertion would do.                       | 2.3           |

# Running E2E tests

There are two Playwright suites.

| Suite         | Runs against                                  | Command           |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `e2e/`        | A disposable Saleor in docker, seeded locally | `pnpm e2e`        |
| `e2e-legacy/` | A provisioned Saleor Cloud instance           | `pnpm e2e:legacy` |

New tests belong in `e2e/`. See [`e2e/README.md`](../e2e/README.md) — it covers the two
Saleor targets (latest stable and unreleased main), how seeds are built and cached, and how
to port a spec across.

## The legacy suite

> [!NOTE]
> `e2e-legacy/` is frozen. It is kept running until its specs have been reviewed and ported
> to `e2e/`; it should not be extended or edited.

It is based on Saleor Cloud and uses snapshots with prepared data. To run it against your
own infrastructure you need to update the test data with your own created objects in
[`e2e-legacy/data/e2eTestData.ts`](../e2e-legacy/data/e2eTestData.ts) and create a snapshot.

Playwright-specific env variables for `.env`:

```
BASE_URL=
API_URL=

E2E_USER_NAME=
E2E_USER_PASSWORD=
E2E_PERMISSIONS_USERS_PASSWORD=

MAILPITURL=
```

Then:

```shell
pnpm run e2e:legacy
```

If you change `BASE_URL` to run against a different environment, clear the login data cached
in `e2e-legacy/.auth`:

```shell
pnpm run e2e:legacy:clean-auth
```

# Review an e2e test against the checklist

Be the reviewer who would otherwise catch this in the pull request. Judge the change, not the
author's explanation of it.

## 1. Collect the change

1. `git status --porcelain` lists what changed. Read every added or modified file under `e2e/`
   in full: the spec, and any page object or scenario it touched. Any change outside `e2e/`
   (above all `src/`) is a finding in itself: a test ticket does not change the app, and a
   locator that depends on such a change is a B6 failure for a reviewer who sees only `e2e/`.
2. Read the ticket the test is for. List its acceptance criteria.
3. Read `CHECKLIST.md`. For the "duplicated helper" check, also read the existing page objects
   in `e2e/pages/`, `e2e/lib/graphql.ts` and the scenario files the spec imports.

## 2. Go through every item

Take each item in `CHECKLIST.md` in order, B1 to B10 and M1 to M13, and decide **met** or
**failed**. For a failure, give the file and line and one sentence on what is wrong. Do not skip
an item because it seems unlikely; most misses are in the items that seemed fine.

The ones that need real work:

- **B1, would pass with the feature broken.** For each assertion, imagine the server ignored the
  action: the mutation never ran, or returned without changing anything. Would the assertion still
  pass? Things the UI does whether or not the server acted - a dialog closing, a navigation the
  client performs, a toast, an input still holding typed text, a button being clicked - do not
  prove the outcome. Values read back after `page.reload()`, or from the API, do. B1 fails if
  some acceptance criterion is only "proved" by assertions of the first kind.
- **B2, acceptance criteria.** Map each criterion to the line that asserts it. A criterion
  without a line is a failure.
- **B3, duplicates.** Search the page objects for the test id or the action before accepting a
  new locator or method.
- **B6, selectors.** Every locator: test id, or role with a name, scoped to its container when the
  id is shared (`submit`, `confirm-button`, `select-option` appear on many screens).
- **B7 and B8, data.** Where does every value the test relies on come from? The scenario's
  exported constants and `findOrderId` are fine; literals that happen to match the seed, ids, and
  API calls that arrange state are not.

## 3. Check it runs

- `pnpm run check-types:e2e`
- `pnpm e2e <spec path> --repeat-each=3`

A type error is B10. A failing or flaky run is reported as such; do not add retries or waits to
make it pass.

## 4. Report

```
Ticket: <id>
Files reviewed: <paths>

Blockers
- B1 met
- B4 FAILED e2e/pages/orderPage.ts:104 waitForTimeout(1000) after saving
...

Minors
- M1 met
...

Runs: check-types clean; 3/3 passed
Verdict: <merge | fix blockers first | fix minors>
```

If you wrote the test yourself, fix every failed item now and review again until no blocker is
left.
